# PART 6 — INDIAN PHYSICAL GEOGRAPHY

**UPPCS Priority: 🔴 VERY HIGH**

This should be one of the **most heavily memorised sections** in your booklet because UPPCS repeatedly tests India through **map-based locations, physiographic divisions, rivers, mountains, soils, drainage, climate, natural vegetation and physical features**.

I am keeping this as a **Ratta Booklet**: facts, numbers, sequences, locations, classifications and one-line associations.

---

# 1. 🇮🇳 INDIA — BASIC PHYSICAL FACTS

| Fact                             | Ratta                                 |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| India lies in                    | **Northern + Eastern Hemispheres**    |
| Latitudinal extent               | **8°4′N–37°6′N**                      |
| Longitudinal extent              | **68°7′E–97°25′E**                    |
| Standard Meridian                | **82°30′E**                           |
| Standard Meridian passes through | **Mirzapur, Uttar Pradesh**           |
| Tropic of Cancer                 | **23°30′N approximately**             |
| Tropic of Cancer passes through  | **8 Indian states**                   |
| Southernmost point of India      | **Indira Point**                      |
| Southernmost point of mainland   | **Kanyakumari**                       |
| Northernmost point               | **Indira Col region**                 |
| Easternmost point                | **Kibithu region, Arunachal Pradesh** |
| Westernmost point                | **Guhar Moti, Gujarat**               |

### 🔴

> **82°30′E → Standard Meridian → Mirzapur**

> **8°4′N → Southern mainland latitude**

> **37°6′N → Northern extent**

# 2. 🌍 TROPIC OF CANCER — INDIA

Tropic of Cancer passes through **8 states**:

> **Gujarat → Rajasthan → Madhya Pradesh → Chhattisgarh → Jharkhand → West Bengal → Tripura → Mizoram**

### Mnemonic

> **G R M C J W T M**

### 🔴

**West → East:**

> Gujarat → Rajasthan → MP → Chhattisgarh → Jharkhand → West Bengal → Tripura → Mizoram

---

# 3. 🇮🇳 INDIA'S MAJOR PHYSIOGRAPHIC DIVISIONS

Six major divisions:

1. **Northern & Northeastern Mountains**
2. **Northern Plains**
3. **Peninsular Plateau**
4. **Indian Desert**
5. **Coastal Plains**
6. **Islands**

### 🔴

> **Mountains → Plains → Plateau → Desert → Coast → Islands**

---

# 4. 🏔️ HIMALAYAN SYSTEM

The Himalayas are:

> **Young fold mountains**

They extend from:

> **Indus → Brahmaputra**

Length approximately:

> **2,400 km**

Width:

> Greater in west; narrower toward east.

### 🔴

> **Himalayas → Young fold mountains**

> **Indus → Brahmaputra**

---

# 5. 🏔️ THREE PARALLEL HIMALAYAN RANGES

From north to south:

> **Himadri → Himachal → Shiwalik**

### 🔴 MASTER RATTA

> **Himadri = Greater Himalaya**

> **Himachal = Lesser/Middle Himalaya**

> **Shiwalik = Outer Himalaya**

---

# 6. 🏔️ HIMADRI

Also:

> **Greater Himalaya**

Characteristics:

* northernmost major Himalayan range
* highest
* most continuous
* contains many highest peaks.

Average elevation:

> **~6,000 m**

### 🔴

> **Himadri → Highest + continuous**

---

# 7. 🏔️ HIMACHAL

Also:

> **Lesser Himalaya / Middle Himalaya**

Contains ranges such as:

> Pir Panjal

> Dhauladhar

> Mahabharat

Characteristics:

> More dissected than Himadri.

Important valleys:

> Kashmir Valley

> Kangra Valley

> Kullu Valley

### 🔴

> **Himachal → Pir Panjal + Dhauladhar**

---

# 8. 🏔️ SHIWALIK

Also:

> **Outer Himalaya**

Southernmost Himalayan range.

Characteristics:

> Lowest + youngest Himalayan range.

Important feature:

> **Duns**

Examples:

> Dehra Dun

> Kotli Dun

> Patli Dun

### 🔴

> **Shiwalik → Duns**

> **Dehra Dun → Dun valley**

---

# 9. 🏔️ DUNS

Longitudinal valleys between:

> **Shiwalik + Lesser Himalaya**

Examples:

> Dehra Dun

> Kotli Dun

> Patli Dun

### 🔴

> **Dun → Valley between Shiwalik and Lesser Himalaya**

# 32. 🌊 BHABAR

Narrow belt:

> **Along Himalayan foothills**

Characteristics:

> Coarse sediments + porous.

Streams:

> Often disappear underground.

### 🔴

> **Bhabar → Pebbles + porous → Streams disappear**

---

# 33. 🌾 TERAI

Located:

> **South of Bhabar**

Characteristics:

> Fine sediments + water re-emerges.

Result:

> Marshy/wet region.

### 🔴

> **Bhabar → streams disappear**

> **Terai → streams reappear**

---

# 34. 🌾 BHANGAR

Older alluvium.

Located:

> **Above floodplains**

Characteristics:

> Relatively old deposits.

Contains:

> **Kankar nodules**

### 🔴

> **Bhangar → Old alluvium → Kankar**

---

# 35. 🌾 KHADAR

Newer alluvium.

Located:

> **Active floodplains**

Renewed by:

> Annual/periodic floods.

### 🔴

> **Khadar → New alluvium → Floodplain**

---

# 36. 🌾 BHANGAR vs KHADAR

| Bhangar                 | Khadar             |
| ----------------------- | ------------------ |
| Older alluvium          | Newer alluvium     |
| Higher surface          | Lower floodplain   |
| Kankar                  | Fresh deposits     |
| Less frequently flooded | Frequently flooded |

### 🔥

> **Bhangar = Old**

> **Khadar = New**

---

# 66. 🌊 WEST COAST VS EAST COAST

| West Coast                   | East Coast                          |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| Narrow                       | Broad                               |
| Western Ghats close to coast | Eastern Ghats farther/discontinuous |
| Estuaries common             | Large deltas common                 |
| Arabian Sea                  | Bay of Bengal                       |
| Backwaters in Kerala         | Deltaic plains                      |

> **West → Estuaries**

> **East → Deltas**

# 73. 🌊 HIMALAYAN RIVERS

Characteristics:

> **Perennial**

Reason:

> Snow/glacier + rainfall.

Generally:

> Long courses + large basins + meandering in plains.

Major systems:

> Indus

> Ganga

> Brahmaputra.

### 🔴

> **Himalayan rivers → Perennial**

---

# 74. 🌊 PENINSULAR RIVERS

Characteristics:

> Mostly seasonal compared with Himalayan rivers.

Sources:

> Mainly rainfall.

Valleys:

> Generally shallower and more fixed courses.

Major:

> Mahanadi

> Godavari

> Krishna

> Kaveri

> Narmada

> Tapi.

---

> Tibet → India → Pakistan

> **Arabian Sea**

Major tributaries:

> Jhelum

> Chenab

> Ravi

> Beas

> Sutlej

> **Five rivers of Punjab → Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej**

# 108. 🏞️ RIVER VALLEY TYPES

### Antecedent rivers

River existed before mountain uplift and maintained course by downcutting.

Examples commonly cited:

> Indus

> Sutlej

> Brahmaputra

### 🔴

> **Antecedent → Himalayas**

---

# 109. 🏞️ SUPERIMPOSED DRAINAGE

River establishes course over younger cover and later cuts into underlying structures.

Important examples:

> Chambal

> Banas

> Some Peninsular drainage examples.

---

# 110. 🏞️ RIFT VALLEY RIVERS

Important:

> **Narmada**

> **Tapi**

Flow through:

> Faulted/rift valleys.

### 🔴

> **Narmada + Tapi → Rift valley**

---

# 111. 🌊 DRAINAGE PATTERNS

### Dendritic

> Tree-like

Develops where:

> Uniform rock structure.

### Trellis

> Main streams + right-angle tributaries.

Associated with:

> Folded/alternating resistant rocks.

### Radial

> Flows outward from central highland.

Example:

> **Amarkantak region**

### Centripetal

> Flows inward toward depression/basin.

Example:

> **Lake basin/desert depression**

### Rectangular

> Right-angle bends due to joints/faults.

### 🔥

> **Dendritic → Uniform rocks**

> **Trellis → Folded/alternating rocks**

> **Radial → Dome/volcanic/highland**

> **Centripetal → Basin/depression**

---

# 113. 🌾 ALLUVIAL SOIL

> **Northern Plains**

> Coastal/deltaic plains.

> Rice + wheat + sugarcane etc.

> Old alluvium.

> **Kankar**

# 116. ⚫ BLACK SOIL

Also:

> **Regur**

Origin:

> **Basaltic Deccan Trap rocks**

Characteristics:

> High clay content

> High moisture retention

> Develops deep cracks on drying.

Best known crop:

> **Cotton**

### 🔥

> **Black soil → Deccan → Basalt → Cotton**

---

# 117. 🔴 RED SOIL

Colour:

> Iron compounds.

Major regions:

> Peninsular India

> Odisha

> Chhattisgarh

> Jharkhand

> Karnataka

> Tamil Nadu etc.

### 🔴

> **Red soil → Iron → Peninsular India**

---

# 118. 🟡 YELLOW SOIL

Red soils may appear:

> Yellow under hydrated conditions.

Association:

> Eastern/southern Peninsular regions.

---

# 119. 🧱 LATERITE SOIL

Develops under:

> **High temperature + heavy rainfall**

Process:

> **Leaching**

Rich in:

> Iron + aluminium.

Major regions:

> Western Ghats

> Eastern Ghats

> Northeast

> parts of Odisha/Jharkhand etc.

### 🔴

> **Laterite → Heavy rain + leaching**

---

# 120. 🏜️ ARID SOIL

Location:

> **Rajasthan + western dry regions**

Characteristics:

> Sandy + low humus.

Often:

> Saline/alkaline.

### 🔴

> **Arid soil → Rajasthan**

---

# 121. 🌲 FOREST/MOUNTAIN SOILS

Location:

> **Himalayas + mountainous regions**

Properties vary with:

> altitude + vegetation + slope.

---

# 122. 🌾 PEATY/MARSHY SOIL

Develops where:

> Waterlogging + high organic matter accumulation.

Regions:

> Wet areas including parts of Kerala, Odisha, West Bengal etc.

### 🔴

> **Peaty → Waterlogging + organic matter**

# 131. 🌧️ INDIA — MAJOR RAINFALL PATTERN

# 132. 🌧️ MEGHALAYA

# 133. 🏜️ WESTERN RAJASTHAN

Low rainfall because:

> Subtropical high pressure + continentality + Aravalli orientation.

### Important

Aravalli runs roughly:

> **SW–NE**

It is not oriented perpendicular enough to effectively block the southwest monsoon across Rajasthan.

# 134. 🌧️ MONSOON & WESTERN GHATS

Moist Arabian Sea branch:

> Hits Western Ghats.

Windward:

> Heavy rainfall.

Leeward:

> Rain shadow.

### 🔴

> **Western Ghats → Orographic rainfall → Deccan rain shadow**
